display.purpose: The h1 inside a transcript. Rare by design.

title.purpose: Transcript h3/h4, form input text, the composer.

body.purpose: Message prose, list items, field values.

label.purpose: Button labels, tab labels, card titles, field labels.

micro.purpose: Tags, badges, timestamps, section headings, meta rows. Never below 11px.

mono.purpose: Every machine-produced string: ids, paths, counts, status, the status strip.

shadows.name: overlay
shadows.purpose: Popovers and toasts only. Neutral, offset, only while open.

shadows.name: modal
shadows.purpose: The modal card inside its scrim.

shadows.name: control-press
shadows.purpose: The selected segment of a switch, lifted one step off its track.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default transition for background, border, and color state changes.

motion.name: anchor-bob
motion.purpose: The anchor mark while a Muse is working. Suppressed under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: caret-blink
motion.purpose: The streaming caret. Suppressed under prefers-reduced-motion.

breakpoints.name: wide
breakpoints.purpose: Sidebar occupies layout space at 280px (440px with Settings open).

breakpoints.name: drawer
breakpoints.purpose: Sidebar becomes an off-canvas drawer over the main column, closed by default, behind a scrim.

breakpoints.name: compact
breakpoints.purpose: Dock and transcript padding compress, brand badge hides, toolbar labels collapse to icons, status strip wraps.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one action in a row. A raised dark plate with violet text, never a saturated fill.

components.name: Secondary Button

components.name: Text Input

components.name: Sidebar Tab
components.description: A sidebar destination. Always labelled in text; the icon is a secondary cue, never the only one.

components.name: File Tree Row
components.description: One row of the workspace tree. Directories carry a chevron, a violet folder mark, the name, and a file count; files carry a neutral document mark and the filename only. Depth is indentation, never truncation.

narrative.overview:
PLUTON is the operator's station on a working vessel. The product is a control plane for a crew of persistent AI Muses; the interface is the bridge you stand on while they work. Everything about the visual language follows from that: instruments that are legible in low light, controls that are within reach, and a horizon that stays visible when the work gets loud. The maritime motif in PLUTON is not decoration — the ship mark, the anchor, the sailing crew — it is the product's honest self-description, and this system extends it rather than restating it.

Quiet instrument, loud state. The interface recedes; only state changes speak. A run that stalls, an approval that arrives, a model that changes, a tool that fails — these earn color, weight, and motion. Everything else stays a dark panel with a hairline seam. This is a dense operator tool, not a consumer product, so the surface area does the quiet work: layered near-black plates, one-pixel rivet lines, monospaced data, and a single violet signal that marks identity rather than decoration.

The system explicitly refuses: neon glow, floating glass cards, rainbow status palettes, and anything that reads as a consumer chatbot. It also refuses ornament without meaning — a gradient that carries no hierarchy, a shadow that expresses no elevation, an emoji that arrives from another product's icon set.
keyCharacteristics: Flat by default, lifted on state.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal Violet marks PLUTON itself and nothing else. If a violet element is not the product, the current selection, or the current Muse, it does not exist. Status colors carry state; they never carry identity.

rules.name: The Luminous Floor Rule
rules.body: The darkest text allowed anywhere is Sea Fog Dim (#8e8a9f) on the darkest plate it ever sits on, and only at 11px or larger. No functional text drops below 4.5:1 against its own background.

rules.name: The No-Glow Rule
rules.body: No chromatic halo, no zero-offset colored shadow, no blurred color bloom. A live state is announced by a solid mark and a word, not by a glow.

rules.name: The Six-Step Ramp Rule
rules.body: The system has exactly six text sizes (11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 17px) and one mono size (12px). Nothing sits between two steps, and nothing sits below 11px.

rules.name: The Mono Means Machine Rule
rules.body: If a string came out of the runtime, it is set in mono. If a human wrote it, it is set in Inter.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. If a component needs to float to be understood, it is not resting — it is an overlay, and overlays are the only things that float.

rules.name: The No-Chromatic-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows are neutral black, never violet, cyan, green, or red, and never zero-offset. A colored halo is a glow, and a glow is a lie about the surface.

dos: Do keep the violet signal scarce: identity, current selection, and the PLUTON mark only.
Do announce state with a word and a mark together, never with color alone.
Do set machine-produced strings in mono and human-written strings in Inter.
Do keep functional text at 11px or larger, and body text at 13px or larger.
Do let overlays be the only floating things on screen.
Do honour prefers-reduced-motion: the anchor bob and the streaming caret stop.
Do draw icons as inline SVG in a single 2px-stroke style, at 14–16px.
donts: Don't use a chromatic glow, a zero-offset colored shadow, or a colored blur. The connection dot is a solid mark, not a bloom.
Don't use emoji as interface icons. The anchor, the folder, the ship, and the warning are SVG marks drawn in the same stroke style as everything else.
Don't put a thick colored bar on the side of a card. A task's state is named in text and shown with a 1px tinted border plus a status word.
Don't run text below 11px, and don't ship a size ramp with more than six steps.
Don't fill a button with Signal Violet at #8b5cf6 and white text; it fails contrast.
Don't let the sidebar cover the transcript at narrow widths. It is off-canvas there.
Don't center the transcript. It is a left-aligned reading column with one stable edge.
